:::{#exr-matvec-practice}
#### A matrix-vector product with more columns than rows

A [matrix-vector product](#def-matvec-mult) $\matr{A}\vx$ computes one [weighted sum](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-weighted-sum) of the entries of $\vx$ for each [row of $\matr{A}$](#def-matrix-row),
so one multiplication computes several weighted sums at once.
The [matrix](#def-matrix) $\matr{A}$ below has more [column](#def-matrix-column)s than [row](#def-matrix-row)s,
so $\matr{A}\vx$ is shorter than $\vx$.
Let

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 5 & 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\vx = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Compute $\matr{A}\vx$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Entry $i$ of $\matr{A}\vx$ is the [dot product](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-dot-product) of the $i$th [row of $\matr{A}$](#def-matrix-row) with $\vx$,
as in @rem-matvec-row-dot-products.

:::
